groups.label: Carpal bones
groups.info: Eight carpal bones. The scaphoid is the one most often broken, and it can be missed on the first X-ray.

groups.label: ___ stones
groups.info: GALLstones, KIDNEY stones, TONSIL stones (tonsilloliths), PULP stones (in teeth), BLADDER stones.

groups.label: Eponymous fractures
groups.info: Colles: wrist, dorsal tilt. Smith: wrist, volar tilt. Barton: wrist rim plus dislocation. Bennett and Rolando: base of the thumb.

groups.label: Nobel Prize in Medicine winners
groups.info: Florey (penicillin) and Burnet (immune tolerance) and Eccles (synapses) were Australian. Banting (insulin) was Canadian, Fleming Scottish.

groups.label: HIV research pioneers
groups.info: Gallo and Montagnier, Barré-Sinoussi (Nobel 2008) found HIV. David Ho pushed combination therapy. David Cooper (Australian) led early HIV trials.

groups.label: Heart failure symptoms and signs
groups.info: PND = paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea: waking up gasping. Orthopnoea: breathless lying flat.

groups.label: Machines that back up the heart
groups.info: LVAD = left ventricular assist device. Intra-aortic balloon pump. ICD shocks dangerous rhythms. Pacemakers fix slow ones.

groups.label: Stand-ins for other body parts
groups.info: Dialysis does the kidney's job, cochlear implants the ear's, joint replacements the joint's, an intraocular lens the eye's own lens (after cataract surgery).

groups.label: Hidden ART
groups.info: Each hides ART: ARTery, cARTilage, pARTogram, heARTburn.

groups.label: Accessibility features
groups.info: A hearing loop sends sound straight to hearing aids set to the T (telecoil) setting.

groups.label: Sign languages
groups.info: Auslan (Australia), ASL (American), BSL (British), NZSL. Auslan, BSL and NZSL share a family; ASL is unrelated.

groups.label: Paralympic champions
groups.info: Tanni Grey-Thompson, Louise Sauvage, Esther Vergeer, Dylan Alcott: wheelchair racing and tennis greats.

groups.label: ___ dog
groups.info: GUIDE dog, SERVICE dog, HEARING dog, HOT dog.

groups.label: Muscle proteins
groups.info: Titin is the largest known human protein. Troponin leaks from damaged heart muscle.

groups.label: Muscle fuel stores
groups.info: ATP lasts seconds, creatine phosphate about 10 seconds, glycogen minutes to hours, fat for the long haul.

groups.label: Medicines modelled on animal venom
groups.info: Captopril: Brazilian pit viper. Eptifibatide: rattlesnake. Ziconotide: cone snail. Exenatide: Gila monster saliva.

groups.label: Start with the Greek for 'fast'
groups.info: Tachy- = fast. Tachyphylaxis: a drug quickly stops working. Tachyzoite: the fast-dividing form of Toxoplasma.

groups.label: Donated by volunteers
groups.info: Australia's Lifeblood collects plasma, platelets and breast milk; bone marrow donors join a registry.

groups.label: Antibiotics from soil bacteria
groups.info: Streptomycin, vancomycin, tetracycline and erythromycin all come from soil actinomycetes.

groups.label: Medicines from moulds and fungi
groups.info: Penicillin (Penicillium), ciclosporin (Tolypocladium), griseofulvin (Penicillium griseofulvum), lovastatin (Aspergillus).

groups.label: ___ bank
groups.info: MEMORY bank, RIVER bank, PIGGY bank, FOOD bank.

groups.label: Health words in another language
groups.info: Finnish: lääkäri = doctor, sairaala = hospital, krapula = hangover, terveyskeskus = health centre.

groups.label: North Karelia Project targets
groups.info: Finland's 1972 North Karelia Project cut heart deaths in working-age men by about 80% over 35 years.

groups.label: Rare inherited diseases from one small nation
groups.info: Part of the 'Finnish disease heritage', about 36 rare diseases common in Finland. AGU = aspartylglucosaminuria.

groups.label: Hidden fish part (FIN)
groups.info: Each hides FIN: FINasteride, paraFFIN, deFINitive, FINger.

groups.label: Parts of a plane
groups.info: The rudder steers left and right; the fuselage is the body.

groups.label: Flying health problems
groups.info: DVT risk rises on flights over about 4 hours. Cabins are pressurised to about 2,400 m, so oxygen levels drop a little.

groups.label: Ways to clear your ears on descent
groups.info: All open the Eustachian tube. Valsalva: pinch your nose, close your mouth, blow gently.

groups.label: ___ pressure
groups.info: AIR pressure, BLOOD pressure, PEER pressure, WATER pressure.

groups.label: Inhaled-dust lung diseases
groups.info: Silica (stone), coal (anthrac-), cotton (byssin-), beryllium, iron (sider-).

groups.label: Nail signs
groups.info: Koilonychia = spoon nails (iron deficiency). Onycholysis = lifting. Leukonychia = white. Pitting = psoriasis. Beau's lines = past severe illness.

groups.label: Signs of endocarditis
groups.info: Osler nodes: painful. Janeway lesions: painless. Roth spots: retina. Splinter haemorrhages under nails.

groups.label: Causes of clubbing
groups.info: Clubbing is never from COPD alone. Think cancer, pus (empyema, abscess, endocarditis), fibrosis, cirrhosis.

groups.label: Start with a fish
groups.info: CARPal, SOLEus, RAYnaud, CODeine, CHARcot.

groups.label: Four principles of biomedical ethics
groups.info: Beauchamp and Childress, 1979: autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, justice.

groups.label: Observational study designs
groups.info: Cohort follows people forward; case-control looks back; cross-sectional is a snapshot; ecological compares groups, not people.

groups.label: Randomised trial designs
groups.info: Crossover: everyone gets both treatments in turn. Factorial: tests two treatments at once. Cluster: randomises groups like practices.

groups.label: Start with a Greek letter
groups.info: PSI-ttacosis, CHI-ckenpox, RHO-dopsin, TAU-opathy.

groups.label: Discoveries that won in Stockholm
groups.info: Nobel Medicine prizes: H. pylori (2005, Marshall and Warren, Perth), prions (1997), HIV (2008), telomerase (2009).

groups.label: Peace Prize winners in health
groups.info: MSF (1999), Albert Schweitzer (1952), Denis Mukwege (2018), Red Cross (three times).

groups.label: Chemistry breakthroughs with a health link
groups.info: All won the Chemistry Nobel: CRISPR 2020, PCR 1993, GFP 2008, phage display 2018.

groups.label: Homophones of award words
groups.info: MEDDLE = medal, PIECE = peace, PRIES = prize, GOALED = gold.

groups.label: Altitude illnesses
groups.info: AMS = acute mountain sickness. HAPE = fluid on the lungs, HACE = brain swelling. Monge's = chronic mountain sickness.

groups.label: How the body adapts to altitude
groups.info: Within hours you breathe harder; over weeks EPO rises and you make more red cells.

groups.label: Everest firsts
groups.info: Hillary and Norgay (1953), Junko Tabei (first woman, 1975), Reinhold Messner (first without oxygen, 1978).

groups.label: Hidden ALP
groups.info: Each hides ALP: pALPitation, scALPel, ALPrazolam, pALPable.

groups.label: WHO health system building blocks
groups.info: WHO's six blocks also include information systems and medicines.

groups.label: Social determinants of health
groups.info: Where people live, learn, earn and work shapes health more than health care does.

groups.label: Isaacs' geriatric giants
groups.info: Bernard Isaacs, 1960s: the 'four I's' of frail older people.

groups.label: Anagrams of organs
groups.info: EARTH → HEART · VILER → LIVER · SLUNG → LUNGS · BAIRN → BRAIN.

groups.label: The Hs of reversible cardiac arrest
groups.info: Four Hs: hypoxia, hypovolaemia, hypothermia, hyper/hypokalaemia (and other metabolic).

groups.label: The Ts of reversible cardiac arrest
groups.info: Four Ts: tamponade, toxins, thrombosis (heart or lung), tension pneumothorax.

groups.label: Resuscitation pioneers
groups.info: Beck: first defibrillation (1947). Zoll: external pacing. Lown: DC cardioversion. Pantridge: first mobile coronary care unit (Belfast).

groups.label: Hidden AMP, not a reversible cause
groups.info: Each hides AMP: crAMP, AMPoule, clAMP, hippocAMPus.

groups.label: The four humours
groups.info: Hippocrates and Galen: illness came from an imbalance of the four humours.

groups.label: Mostly abandoned treatments
groups.info: Bloodletting survives only for a few conditions, such as haemochromatosis.

groups.label: Causes of a severe sore throat
groups.info: Epiglottitis and quinsy can block the airway. Drooling and muffled voice are red flags.

groups.label: Blood ___
groups.info: BLOOD ORANGE, BLOODHOUND, BLOOD MOON, BLOOD DIAMOND.

groups.label: Vitamins
groups.info: B1 thiamine, B2 riboflavin, B3 niacin, B12 cobalamin, A retinol.

groups.label: Deficiency diseases
groups.info: Scurvy (vitamin C), beriberi and Wernicke (B1), pellagra (B3), rickets (vitamin D).

groups.label: Explorers
groups.info: Cook, Drake, Magellan, Tasman, Columbus. Scurvy killed more sailors than battles did.

groups.label: Eponymous neuroanatomy
groups.info: Broca's area, circle of Willis, Sylvian fissure, Rolandic fissure, foramen of Monro.

groups.label: Hide a vehicle
groups.info: CARtilage, BUSulfan, VANcomycin, CABergoline, TRAMadol.

groups.label: Hearing tests
groups.info: Weber and Rinne use a 512 Hz tuning fork to tell conductive from sensorineural loss.

groups.label: Causes of hearing loss
groups.info: Presbycusis: age-related, high pitches first. Otosclerosis: stapes fixes in place.

groups.label: Composers who lost their hearing
groups.info: Beethoven, Smetana, Fauré and Vaughan Williams all kept composing after losing hearing.

groups.label: -phobias that are symptoms, not fears
groups.info: Phonophobia (sound) and photophobia (light) in migraine; osmophobia (smell); hydrophobia in rabies.

groups.label: Aviation pioneers
groups.info: Amelia Earhart, the Wright brothers, Louis Blériot, Bessie Coleman (first Black woman pilot).

groups.label: Flying Doctor pioneers
groups.info: Royal Flying Doctor Service, 1928: John Flynn's idea, Alfred Traeger's pedal radio, Arthur Affleck flew, Dr Kenyon St Vincent Welch was first doctor.

groups.label: Gas laws
groups.info: Boyle (pressure-volume), Dalton (partial pressures), Henry (gas dissolving: the bends), Charles (volume-temperature).

groups.label: Hidden AIR
groups.info: Each hides AIR: hAIRline fracture, dAIRy, stAIRs, despAIR.

groups.label: Vaccines often needing catch-up
groups.info: Catch-up vaccines are free in Australia for refugees and some migrants.

groups.label: New-arrival refugee health screen
groups.info: Screening after arrival often includes TB, hepatitis B and C, HIV, strongyloides and malaria.

groups.label: Neglected tropical diseases
groups.info: Chagas (kissing bugs), leishmaniasis (sandflies), trachoma (leading infectious blindness), Buruli ulcer (also in Victoria).

groups.label: Hidden countries
groups.info: inCUBAtor, abnorMALIty, MALTAse, wOMAN.

groups.label: Retrospective diagnoses for Tiny Tim
groups.info: Dickens never named it. Rickets and TB are the old favourites; renal tubular acidosis was proposed in 1992.

groups.label: Victorian occupational diseases
groups.info: Phossy jaw: white phosphorus in match factories. Potter's rot: silicosis. Woolsorter's disease: anthrax.

groups.label: Victorian public-health reformers
groups.info: Edwin Chadwick (sanitation), William Farr (statistics), John Simon (medical officer), William Duncan (first UK medical officer of health).

groups.label: Hide Tiny Tim backwards
groups.info: TIM backwards is MIT: voMITing, interMITtent, heMIThorax, MITral.

groups.label: Global health organisations
groups.info: Gavi buys vaccines for poorer countries; UNICEF delivers many of them.

groups.label: Walls of the whare in Te Whare Tapa Whā
groups.info: Mason Durie's Māori health model: tinana (body), hinengaro (mind), whānau (family), wairua (spirit).

groups.label: WHO Directors-General
groups.info: Halfdan Mahler, Gro Harlem Brundtland, Margaret Chan, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus.

groups.label: Hidden UNITY
groups.info: Each hides UNITY: immUNITY, commUNITY, impUNITY, opportUNITY.

groups.label: Stress hormones
groups.info: ACTH from the pituitary tells the adrenals to make cortisol.

groups.label: Sleep science
groups.info: N3 is deep sleep. Melatonin rises in the dark and sets your circadian clock.

groups.label: Relaxation practices
groups.info: Box breathing: in 4, hold 4, out 4, hold 4.

groups.label: Hidden ZEN
groups.info: Each hides ZEN: froZEN shoulder, benZENe, doZEN, citiZEN.

groups.label: Santa's reindeer
groups.info: Rudolph joined the team later, in a 1939 story.

groups.label: Santa, by other names
groups.info: Kris Kringle, St Nicholas, Santa Claus, Père Noël (France), Sinterklaas (Netherlands).

groups.label: Clotting factors, by name
groups.info: Factor I fibrinogen, II prothrombin, XII Hageman, IX Christmas, X Stuart-Prower.

groups.label: Famous Rudolfs
groups.info: Rudolf Virchow (pathology, Virchow's triad), Nureyev, Valentino, Diesel (engine), Clausius (entropy).

groups.label: Hide an organ
groups.info: COLONel, LIVERpool, HEARTh, LUNGe, GUTter.

groups.label: Anti-rejection drugs
groups.info: Tacrolimus and ciclosporin are calcineurin inhibitors.

groups.label: Parts of the nephron
groups.info: Bowman's capsule, loop of Henle, macula densa (senses salt).

groups.label: Surgical pioneers
groups.info: Joseph Murray: first kidney transplant (twins, 1954). Starzl: liver. Barnard: heart. Calne: introduced ciclosporin.

groups.label: Kidney ___
groups.info: KIDNEY BEAN, KIDNEY STONE, KIDNEY DISH, steak and KIDNEY PIE.

groups.label: Christmas Eve emergency regulars
groups.info: Button batteries can burn through the oesophagus in 2 hours. Call 13 11 26 (Poisons) straight away.

groups.label: Units of energy
groups.info: 1 food Calorie (kcal) = 4.184 kJ. Therm and BTU are heating units.

groups.label: Energy-bearing parts of the diet
groups.info: Per gram: fat 37 kJ, alcohol 29 kJ, protein and carbohydrate 17 kJ.

groups.label: Hidden ERG
groups.info: Each hides ERG: allERGy, ERGometer, synERGy, ERGot.

groups.label: Mildly toxic festive plants
groups.info: Mostly cause tummy upset. Poinsettia's danger is overrated.

groups.label: Nursing pioneers
groups.info: Clara Barton (US Red Cross), Florence Nightingale, Mary Seacole, Edith Cavell.

groups.label: Clotting factor nicknames
groups.info: Factor IX Christmas (first patient Stephen Christmas), XII Hageman, X Stuart-Prower, XI Rosenthal.

groups.label: Christmas tree ___
groups.info: Christmas tree CATARACT (sparkly crystals), BLADDER (neurogenic, on a cystogram), PATTERN (pityriasis rosea rash), ADAPTER (oxygen tubing).

groups.label: A famous scientific family
groups.info: The Curies: Marie and Pierre, daughter Irène (Nobel too), daughter Eve (writer).

groups.label: Unstable elements
groups.info: Marie Curie found polonium and radium. Curium is named after the Curies.

groups.label: External-beam radiotherapy
groups.info: Linac = linear accelerator. Gamma Knife focuses cobalt beams on the brain. Protons stop at a set depth.

groups.label: Boxing Day punches
groups.info: JAB, HOOK, CROSS, UPPERCUT. Boxing Day isn't named after boxing (it's for Christmas boxes).

groups.label: Outbreak maths
groups.info: R0 = how many people one case infects. Seroprevalence = share with antibodies.

groups.label: Pandemics in history
groups.info: Black Death (1340s) killed about a third of Europe. Antonine Plague (165 AD) was probably smallpox.

groups.label: Bradford Hill criteria
groups.info: Bradford Hill (1965): signs that a link is causal. Temporality (cause before effect) is the only must-have.

groups.label: Hidden RAT
groups.info: Each hides RAT: respiRATion, perfoRATion, sepaRATion, migRATion.

groups.label: X-Men
groups.info: Wolverine, Storm, Cyclops, Rogue.

groups.label: Types of gene mutation
groups.info: A frameshift is an insertion or deletion not in multiples of three, which scrambles the rest of the gene.

groups.label: Real biology, superhero vibes
groups.info: Hyperthymesia: near-total memory of your life. Tetrachromacy: a 4th colour cone. Myostatin deficiency: big muscles.

groups.label: ___ man
groups.info: IRON MAN, ANT-MAN, SPIDER-MAN, BATMAN.

groups.label: Types of tremor
groups.info: Essential tremor: action, often better with alcohol. Resting tremor: Parkinson's. Intention tremor: cerebellum.

groups.label: Types of exercise
groups.info: Eccentric exercise works muscles while they lengthen (lowering a weight).

groups.label: Types of amnesia
groups.info: Anterograde: can't form new memories. Retrograde: lose old ones. Infantile: nobody remembers being a baby.

groups.label: Types of aphasia
groups.info: Expressive = Broca's. Receptive = Wernicke's. Conduction: can't repeat. Anomic: word-finding.

groups.label: Hide a month
groups.info: FEBrile, MARfan, AUGmentin, OCTreotide, NOVocaine.

groups.label: Golf scores
groups.info: Birdie = 1 under par, eagle = 2 under, bogey = 1 over.

groups.label: Classic endometriosis symptoms
groups.info: Dyschezia = pain opening bowels. Average diagnosis takes about 6.5 years in Australia.

groups.label: Injuries named after athletes
groups.info: Golfer's elbow: inner elbow tendon. Jumper's knee: patellar tendon. Skier's thumb: torn thumb ligament (UCL).

groups.label: Hidden golf kit
groups.info: CLUBfoot, envIRONment, commitTEE, sPUTTERing.

groups.label: Folk hangover cures
groups.info: No folk cure works. Water, food and time do.

groups.label: Oesophageal eponyms and disorders
groups.info: Boerhaave: full oesophageal tear. Mallory-Weiss: mucosal tear from vomiting. Barrett: acid changes the lining.

groups.label: Alcohol withdrawal signs
groups.info: Withdrawal starts 6–24 hours after the last drink. Seizures peak at 24–48 hours.

groups.label: Hidden EVE
groups.info: Each hides EVE: sleEVE, bEVErage, sEVErity, elEVEn.
